instruction:
Research Zotero documentation for a researcher who wants one paper listed under two projects, a continuously updating to-read list and a way to review suspected duplicate records. Open Collections and Tags, Searching, and Duplicate Detection. Explain how ordinary collections differ from saved searches and what deleting a collection does to its items; name the three Quick Search modes and distinguish which can include indexed attachment text. State how an Advanced Search changes from matching every condition to matching any condition and what a saved search stores. For duplicates, identify the main matching fields, whether detection crosses libraries, and why the documentation recommends merging instead of deleting a record. Finish by matching each of the three researcher needs to the documented feature, with citations to all three pages. Do not sign in, create a library or change any records.

Stopping condition: Stop when the three-page comparison and need-to-feature recommendations cover collection deletion, search modes and criteria, saved-search behavior and duplicate review without changing any library.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.criterion: Explain differences and deletion effect for collections
items.description: Explain how ordinary collections differ from saved searches and state what deleting a collection does to its items based on the 'Collections and Tags' documentation. Full credit for accurately retrieving these details, or clearly stating if the documentation no longer provides this information. Partial credit if one detail is missing or inaccurate despite being available.

Name the three Quick Search modes and identify which mode can include indexed attachment text based on the 'Searching' documentation. Full credit for naming all three modes correctly and specifying the correct mode for attachment text, or reporting if the documentation has changed. Partial credit if some modes are missing or the attachment text detail is incorrect.

items.criterion: Explain Advanced Search and Saved Search behavior
items.description: State how an Advanced Search changes from matching every condition to matching any condition, and explain what a saved search stores based on the documentation. Full credit for accurately answering both parts, or correctly identifying if the information is unavailable. Partial credit if only one part is answered correctly.

Identify the main matching fields for duplicates, whether detection crosses libraries, and why the documentation recommends merging instead of deleting based on the 'Duplicate Detection' page. Full credit for answering all three aspects correctly, or noting if any aspect is undocumented. Partial credit for answering 1-2 aspects correctly.

Correctly match the three researcher needs to the appropriate features: listing a paper in two projects (Collections), a continuously updating to-read list (Saved Searches), and reviewing suspected duplicates (Duplicate Detection). Full credit if all three are accurately matched based on the gathered information. Partial credit if only 1-2 are matched correctly.

Include citations or URLs to the accessed documentation pages (Collections and Tags, Searching, and Duplicate Detection). Full credit for citing the pages that were successfully accessed. Partial credit for missing citations for pages that were utilized.

Do not sign in, create a library, or change any records. Full credit if the agent successfully operates in a read-only manner without attempting to log in, create accounts, or modify data. No credit if the agent violates these constraints.
